skill.name: devtools
skill.description: Drop-in inspector panel for any json-render app. Use when the user wants to debug a generative UI, inspect the spec tree, edit state at runtime, see dispatched actions, follow stream patches live, browse a catalog, or pick DOM elements to find their spec keys. Triggers include "add devtools", "debug json-render", "inspect the spec", "why is this element not rendering", "see the state at runtime", or requests to tap streams / capture action logs for `@json-render/devtools`.
skill.summary: Integrate json-render devtools to inspect specs, edit runtime state, trace actions, and observe streamed UI updates.
skill.author: vercel-labs

content.user_title: Debug json-render Apps with an Inspector Panel
content.value_statement: Generative interfaces can make rendering errors, state changes, and streamed updates difficult to trace. This skill guides devtools integration and inspection workflows for json-render apps.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation and provider integration for React, Vue, Svelte, and Solid adapters.
Explains spec tree inspection, validation warnings, catalog browsing, and DOM element picking.
Documents runtime state editing and action timelines with parameters, results, errors, and duration.
Shows stream inspection and server-side JSON or YAML stream tap APIs.
Explains shared providers and namespaced state for multiple renderers on one page.
Documents docking controls, layout offsets, event buffers, and the React imperative API.
limitations: Requires an existing json-render application and separately installed core and framework adapter packages.
The imperative hook API is documented only for React.
Catalog browsing requires a catalog prop, and multi-renderer state paths must avoid collisions.
The skill contains documentation only; dependency behavior and production safeguards are not independently verified here.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing UI Elements
use_cases.description: Integrate the inspector to examine spec structure, visibility, and validation warnings when a generated component does not appear.

use_cases.title: Trace Chat UI Streams
use_cases.description: Connect shared providers and message history to inspect stream patches and separate state across generated conversation turns.

use_cases.title: Reproduce State and Action Issues
use_cases.description: Use runtime state editing and action timelines to investigate unexpected transitions in a development environment.

prompt_templates.title: Add the Inspector
prompt_templates.prompt: Add json-render devtools to my existing React app. Identify the provider and install the matching adapter before placing the inspector.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Missing Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Help debug a missing element in my json-render interface. Use the spec tree, validation warnings, visibility settings, and current state.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Inspector Docking
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure devtools for my app with a fixed bottom composer. Use right docking and review reserved space and CSS offsets for overlap.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Multiple Streamed Renderers
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate devtools into my multi-turn json-render chat with one shared provider and namespaced state. Connect message history and a bounded server-side stream tap. Keep sensitive content out of telemetry.

output_examples.input: Where should I place devtools in my Vue json-render app?
output: Install the devtools core package and Vue adapter.
Place the inspector inside the existing JSONUIProvider beside the renderer.
Pass the current spec and provide a catalog for catalog browsing.

output_examples.input: My fixed chat composer overlaps the bottom inspector.
output: Use right docking for a layout with a fixed bottom composer.
Disable dock toggling when the application supports only that position.
Use the published CSS offsets for fixed elements that still need space.

output_examples.input: How do I stop state collisions across generated chat turns?
output: Keep one top-level provider and shared state store.
Prefix each turn's element keys and state paths with a unique message identifier.
Pass the latest spec to the Spec panel and all messages to the Stream panel.

best_practices: Match the framework adapter to the host renderer and place the inspector inside the existing provider.
Namespace state paths and element keys for each generated chat turn.
Use test data, review captured events for sensitive content, and verify production behavior before deployment.
anti_patterns: Wrapping every chat renderer in a separate state provider when the inspector needs shared state.
Reusing state paths across generated messages without unique namespaces.
Forwarding raw state, action parameters, or stream content to telemetry without reviewing sensitive data.

faq.question: Which frameworks does the skill cover?
faq.answer: It documents React, Vue, Svelte, and Solid adapters for json-render.

faq.question: Does the inspector run in production?
faq.answer: The documentation says the component renders null when NODE_ENV is production. Verify this behavior in your build before deployment.

faq.question: Can I edit application state?
faq.answer: The State panel supports inline edits at JSON Pointer paths through the application state store.

faq.question: Can one inspector cover multiple renderers?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented setup uses one shared provider, separate renderer specs, and namespaced state paths.

faq.question: Can I capture events on the server?
faq.answer: The skill shows a bounded event store with JSON stream tapping and names a YAML equivalent. Review captured content before persistence or telemetry.

faq.question: What does this skill install by itself?
faq.answer: The skill is documentation, not an installer. It provides npm commands and integration examples for separately distributed packages.
